newsitem.title: USA: St. Louis elects Harmon as mayor.
newsitem.headline: St. Louis elects Harmon as mayor.

text.p: Former police chief Clarence Harmon was elected mayor of St. Louis Tuesday, defeating two opponents for the post.

Harmon, 57, had all but assured himself of victory a month ago when he won the Democratic primary by defeating first-term Mayor Freeman Bosley Jr. The city has not elected a Republican mayor since 1945.

With most of the votes counted, Harmon had won 72 percent. His nearest rival was Alderman Marit Clark, a Democrat who ran as an independent, with 23 percent, followed by the Republican candidate, Jay Dearing, who got about 5 percent.
Harmon declared victory, saying he was "ready to begin the healing process" following primary and general election campaigns with racial overtones.

Harmon was the city's first black police chief and Bosley its first black mayor. But Harmon had been criticized by some black groups who questioned his record as chief and cast him as a white establishment choice. After last month's primary, Bosley's father, Alderman Freeman Bosley Sr., called Harmon a "rented Negro," the tool of white interests.
The younger Bosley, however, endorsed Harmon last week, saying he was doing so in the interest of Democratic party unity.

Harmon became the first black chief in the 130-year history of the police department in 1991, and retired in 1995 after 27 years. During his time as chief, the local chapter of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People said the police department had a double standard that treated white police better than blacks.
